commenti.body:
Really like this. I feel uncomfortable with the predominant analysis of The Killer being one of complete self reflection of Fincher and his career. While it's very easy to read into it like that, it totally bypasses analysis like this of more of a societal focus.

(Spoilers below)

I almost want to read into it from a capitalist critique perspective. You're buying into a system of complete individualism. Where you have to narrow your view into what's in front of you and why you do it. Ignoring anything outside of that. Making it about what you tell yourself to keep going. He's a complete hypocrite and betrays his own mantra constantly, but it's this which justifies his actions.

I definitely think the capitalist critique was an intended read of the film, you don't start your film in specifically an abandoned WeWork office without being aware of the implications that has for the subsequent film as a whole and its views on capitalism. It almost feels like Fincher returning to some of the themes he explored in Fight Club in that sense (although I'd have to rewatch them both to draw a more direct comparison).

It's absolutely a capitalist critique. One that ends with drinks by the pool at an expensive resort for our complicit protagonist. Mr Fincher knows exactly where he sits within the economic hierarchy: an expensive gun for hire expected to pull off hits for those who own the means of production. Sometimes he misses. But hey, life's still pretty good regardless. Cheers!

"Each and every step of the way, ask yourself, 'What's in it for me?' This is what it takes. What you must commit yourself to. If you want to succeed. Simple."

Absolutely. I think it's really important what goes said and unsaid in his inner thoughts. His philosophy about life also seems to be all over the place and superficial.

I like the thought that the Killer is kind of like a filmmaker, but I just don't get much out of that interpretation. Also I think Fincher would never make a movie about himself haha
Definitely. There are references to corporations everywhere in the movie. I was surprised that he seemed to be making another movie about "the system".
I loved that he's in that position at the end of the film and there's still a sense of intense paranoia, the way a curtain moves in the background, their body language, the way his face twitches.
I loved that he's in that position at the end of the film and there's still a sense of intense paranoia, the way a curtain moves in the background, their body language, the way his face twitches.

WARNING: SPOILERS:

He was aware he messed up, and what the consequences of messing up were, and that for $150k extra everything is scrubbed clean, hell - he had probably handled a few prior fuck-ups before now considering his experience in the game, yet made zero attempt to warn his wife of potential danger, even after noticing a suspicious man with striped socks in the plane and making arrangements to avoid him by delaying his flight voluntarily.

Then he’s somehow gobsmacked that he returns to find a house wrecked and a wife nearly beaten to death, as if he couldn’t believe that the lawyer had sold him out for the extra payday - the slime-ball lawyer being a man literally dealing in death for money, not a care in the world who was the target as long as it meant a payday, yet he assumed he was somehow special and it wouldn’t happen to him. 

For an assassin, he sure was sloppy. Yes he mentioned super-duper tactics like radiation poisoning and such, but did he use anything of the sort? Nope, just the Glock. He disnt even kill the dog, just fed it sleeping tablets, ended up in a fistfight with florida guy, nearly got shanked by the skinny q-tip, and just made a whole series of unbelievable fuck ups.

And as for the rest of the assassins having their details on a rolodex with real actual addresses and stuff, that was just comical. 

If he’d have actually bothered to have a decent backup plan, and warned his wife. The next scene would be the final one by the pool. 

If he’d have shot the florida guy and his mates with a spray of bullets, or planted something on their car whilst they were at the casino, or gone into his house whilst they were at the casino, dealt with the dog, then rigged the house to blow via the gas line or something he would have saved hinself a load of aggro. 

And as for the q-tip, bloody hell, less chat, less whiskey, more “ello, bang”. 

Just didn’t make sense how this guy is supposed to be a good assassin living by his moral code, and by the end of it i was thinking he was just some mental dude thinking he was a top-shelf shooter but was actually a constant fuck-up of a person and that the rest of the assassins just had enough of him and wanted him offed haha.
You made almost all the right points - and for those points I liked the movie. Like everyone of us, his actions and his 'mantra' doesn't align. And like all of us, he stays oblivious of that fact.
Well said, I think it's probably the closest to Fight Club of all things in his filmography
